text:
Liam T: Hi team - I had to go to the ER in Denver last week for a bad allergic reaction. Hospital was in-network but I just got a surprise bill from an emergency physician who says they9re out-of-network. I thought ERs were protected from balance billing?
Benefits Team: Sorry that happened, Liam. The No Surprises Act generally protects patients from out-of-network emergency facility care, but there are a few nuances when individual clinicians bill separately. Can you upload the hospital EOB and the separate physician bill? Also the date of service and claim numbers help.
Liam T: Uploaded EOB and the physician invoice here: https://redwood-cloud/internal-uploads/claims/1842106789-er-eob.pdf and https://redwood-cloud/internal-uploads/claims/1842106789-er-physician-bill.pdf Date: 2026-04-02 Claim# HSP-8871 / PHY-9942
benefits-bot: Automated guidance: For out-of-network ER physician bills when the facility is in-network, members are typically protected from balance billing for emergency services under federal law. To request protection, submit a surprise-billing dispute to carrier including EOBs, itemized bills, and a statement that services were emergency. See: https://docs.redwood.com/benefits/surprise-billing (internal).
Priya S: Quick checklist for us to submit to carrier and, if needed, the independent dispute resolution (IDR) process:
``
- Hospital EOB showing in-network facility
- Itemized physician bill (PHY-9942)
- Medical record or ED discharge summary indicating emergency
- Member statement describing symptoms and that you went to nearest ER
- Any prior authorization (not required for emergencies)
```
Liam T: I can get the ED discharge summary from the hospital portal. I definitely went to the nearest ER and it was a clear emergency.
Carrier Liaison: Thanks Liam. Please DM the medical records once you have them. We'll re-adjudicate the physician claim as a coordinated emergency service. If carrier still pays at out-of-network rate, we can escalate to IDR under the No Surprises Act. That process can take several weeks.
Legal Counsel: Adding legal note: keep all correspondence and do not pay the balance while dispute is active. If provider threatens collection, notify benefits and legal immediately. There are consumer protections and potential penalties for improper balance billing.
Liam T: Provider sent a collection letter yesterday. Should I call them or send something in writing?
Benefits Team: Don't call to make a payment. Send a short written response to the provider billing office referencing that the service was an emergency at an in-network facility and that a dispute is open. We can draft a template if you want.
Priya S: Template we usually send (paste into email to provider billing):
``
To: Billing Office 
Re: PHY-9942 
I, Liam T (member ID XXXXX432), received emergency care on 04/02/2026 at [Hospital Name], an in-network facility. I dispute the balance bill from Dr. X because this was emergency care and I was treated at an in-network facility. Please suspend collection activity and direct billing questions to benefits@redwood.com.
Sincerely,
Liam T
```
Liam T: Please draft and I'll send it. Also, what's the carrier timeline for reprocessing?
Carrier Liaison: Once we have the medical records and both EOBs, we will review internally and aim to reprocess within 7-14 business days. If we still deny balance-billing protection, we will provide appeal options and start IDR if member requests.
Benefits Team: We've opened case BR-9110 and will collect the docs. Liam - please DM the discharge summary and authorize us to speak with the provider billing office (we'll use your written statement as authorization).
Liam T: DM sent and I authorized Redwood benefits team to speak to the provider.
benefits-bot: Reminder: Under the No Surprises Act, patients are not required to pay the difference between billed and allowed amounts for emergency services at in-network facilities. If you do pay, keep receipts and we can pursue reimbursement.
Legal Counsel: If carrier declines and provider persists, next steps: 1) file IDR request (carrier or provider can initiate); 2) contact state DOI if local balance-billing protections apply; 3) escalate to company's legal benefits counsel. We'll coordinate on escalation.
Liam T: Appreciate the help. One small thing  will this affect my premiums or network status?
Benefits Team: No, balance-billing disputes and IDR outcomes do not change your plan tier or premiums. This is a payment dispute between provider and carrier.
Liam T: Thanks everyone, will wait for update. :thumbsup:
